original: "Whoever paid me. Then the men who'd have to keep it fed after I'd gone home." I nodded up at the tank on its legs. "That fills itself out of a stream and a bit of weather. What I'd put in her would want a man's whole attention, and it would want it every day, and the first day it went without, you'd be standing here just the same. Only later, and further from a town."
revised: "Whoever paid me. Then the men who'd have to keep it in order after I'd gone home." I nodded up at the tank on its legs. "That fills itself out of a stream and a bit of weather. What I'd put in her would want a man's whole attention, and it would want it every day, and the first day it went without, you'd be standing here just the same. Only later, and further from a town."

original: "There's use in it. There's no bargain in it, here." I put my hands in my pockets, because they were cold and because it was easier than saying the rest. "Shorten her grade by a foot in the hundred and you'd save more than I could."

original: The answer never changes, because the arithmetic never does. Put one of the few hands that can do the work into an engine and you have bought an engine and lost a bridge, or a mine, or a harbour wall. Iron and fire and water never run out, and they never want tending by a man who took twenty years to make. That is the whole of why the country runs on coal and not on us, and there is no failure of anybody's imagination in it. It is a sum, and an honest sum comes out the same every time.

She never once appeared to look up from the glass she was drying.

"Wainford road," she said.

"It is."

"Four days on it, by the boots." She put the glass on the shelf and took another off the rack. "You'll have come about the hill."

original: I said I had come a fair way to get somewhere nobody remembered anything about me at all. He laughed at that, one short breath, and said that in that case I had chosen my valley badly.

original: I set my bags down under the window. I got my boots off and set them where I would fall over them in the morning, which is where I have always set them. I did not take my coat off. Then I put the candle out.

original: The path was not steep and not long, half an hour from the last of the houses, and it took the stiffness out of my legs and gave me back a clean plain ache instead. It was a cold bright morning still, the dew not off the grass and an edge on the air the climb was glad of. I went up slowly. There was no one to watch me do it and no reason on earth to hurry.
